name: Ethical Poetic Reordering
source_tutorial: knowledge/research/transcripts/what not to do in editing.txt
use_when: A documentary sequence is chronological but repetitive or emotionally flat.
Moving lines or events would create a clearer truthful arc.
Interview sentences can be reordered to preserve meaning and improve comprehension.
avoid_when: Reordering changes factual meaning, causality, chronology, consent, or stakes.
The project requires strict chronology for journalistic, legal, or user-requested reasons.
The rearrangement would make a participant appear to say or experience something untrue.

timeline_pattern.story_rule: Reordering should clarify the real story, not manufacture a false one.
timeline_pattern.debate_rule: For sensitive documentary, mark reordered events or lines for human review.

motion.rule: No special motion rule; avoid transitions that hide ethically significant time jumps.

sound.rule: Preserve speaker intent and natural continuity when moving interview lines.
sound.avoid: Audio edits that make a speaker sound like they said a new claim.

captions.rule: Captions must match the reordered audio exactly and should not create a misleading paraphrase.

color.rule: Grade continuity should not be used to conceal a reorder that materially changes time or place.

implementation.ffmpeg: Track source timestamps in the EDL so reordered clips remain auditable.
implementation.remotion: Keep source metadata for original order, edited order, and reason for reorder.
implementation.blender: Only relevant for animated reconstructions; label or structure time jumps clearly.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Keep original clip order notes before rearranging documentary events.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers or sequence notes to flag reordered interview lines/events for review.

common_mistakes: Moving events to increase tension while changing what actually happened.
Reordering interview lines so a speaker appears to make a different claim.
Failing to flag ethical edits for review.
qc: Does the reorder preserve factual truth and speaker intent?
Would a participant object that the edit changed what happened?
Has any sensitive reorder been flagged for human review?
